 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 None for the petitioner.
Shri  Harish Sharma Dy Ga appearing on behalf of Advocat  ORDER
This is 4th application under Section 483 of BNS (Section 439 of Cr.P.C.) for grant of bail.
Earlier third application had been dismissed on merits on 4.3.2025.

The applicant has been arrested on 7.1.2024 in connection with Crime No.10/2024 registered at Police Station City Kotwali, District Bhind for offence under Sections 420, 409, 467, 468 of IPC read with section 43,66, 66 C of IT (Amendment) Act, 2008.
None for the applicant.

Learned counsel for the respondent/State has submitted that the third application which was dismissed was preferred on the ground of delay in trial and after due consideration it was dismissed on 4th March, 2025.

He further submits that though similar ground has been raised in the present application, however, no order-sheet of the Trial Court has been filed to demonstrate that there is delay in trial at the behest of the prosecution.
Thus, the present application deserves to be dismissed as there are no changed circumstances.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17012 2 MCRC-19237-2025
Heard the counsel for the respondent/State and perused the case diary.

sentences.text: As regards the submission that no prosecution witness is examined till date, no copy of order sheets of the Trial Court or other documents have been filed by applicant on record.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and perusal of material available on record, this Court does not find any substantial change in circumstances after dismissal of second application.
Hence, without commenting anything on merits of the case, the application is dismissed.
Similar is the situation herein.

No copies of the order-sheets of the Trial Court or any other documents have been filed by the applicant to demonstrate that no prosecution witnesses till date has been examined and there is delay in trial that too due to prosecution.

Thus, in absence of aforesaid proceedings prima facie it cannot be said that the delay has been caused at the instance of the prosecution and according to this court there is no changed circumstances to hear this bail application on merits again.
Accordingly, the present bail application is hereby dismissed.
(MILIND RAMESH PHADKE) JUDGE (aspr)
